core_requirements: No — an interface is a reference type, not a class.

content.question_text: Can you declare variables of an interface type?

core_requirements: Yes — you can declare interface variables (e.g., List<String> list).

content.question_text: To what kind of object must an interface variable refer?

core_requirements: It must refer to an object of a class that implements that interface.
acceptable_variations: To an object that implements the interface.

Can an interface extend another interface?

core_requirements: Yes — interfaces support multiple inheritance through extension.

content.question_text: What does extending interfaces allow in terms of inheritance?

core_requirements: It allows multiple chains of inheritance that go from a greater degree of generality to a greater degree of specialization.

content.question_text: Can you supply constants in an interface?
What is the default modifier for static fields (constants) declared in an interface?

core_requirements: They are implicitly public static final.

content.question_text: Can a class implement only one interface?

core_requirements: No — a class can implement multiple interfaces.

content.question_text: Can records and enumerations implement interfaces?

core_requirements: Yes — both records and enums can implement interfaces.
